newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks edge up after three-day decline.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks edge up after three-day decline.

text.p: Lima stocks edged up slightly overall on Thursday as investors made cautious and selective buys among attractively-priced leaders after a three-day decline, brokers said.
They expected the moderate upward tendency to continue on Friday, adding next week's price moves hinged on third quarter corporate results.
"We expect today's tendency to be extended so that the week closes with encouraging indicators for next week," said Pablo Navarro, of Fortuna brokerage.
In Thursday's session, the General Index gained a nominal 0.08 percent to 1,542 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL advanced 0.36 percent to 2,103.1.
"The prices had fallen a lot, so we expected a recovery," said Alejandro Arrieta, of Divisas y Valores. "This small rise comes after a lot of falls."
Total market volume was a low 27.6 million soles ($10.8 million) on 2,028 trades, as overall 33 stocks fell, 31 were flat and 18 gained.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for the largest share of market volume, 12.88 percent, ending up 0.89 percent to 5.68 soles on 625,887 shares.
The mining sector performed strongly, with Minsur up 3.53 percent to 23.5 soles on 124,643 soles, and Atacocha gaining 10.87 percent to 0.51 soles on 2.4 million shares.
Brewery Backus y Johnston lost 0.78 percent to 2.56 soles on 744,499 shares, while another beer company, Compania Nacional de Cerveza, ended down 0.66 percent to 1.51 soles on 728,264 shares.
